pr_body:
The `Timeout` object in Node.js has a `refresh` method, used to restart `setTimeout`/`setInterval` timers. Before this commit, `Timeout.refresh` was not handled, leading to memory leaks when using `fetch` in Node.js. This issue arose because `undici` (the Node.js fetch implementation) uses a refreshed `setTimeout` for cleanup operations.

For reference, see: https://github.com/nodejs/undici/blob/1dff4fd9b1b2cee97c5f8cf44041521a62d3f133/lib/util/timers.js#L45

Fixes: #56586

issue_context.title: Memory leakage in SSR while using native node fetch
issue_context.body:
### Which @angular/* package(s) are the source of the bug?

ssr

### Is this a regression?

Yes

### Description

After upgrading our enterprise application to NG17, we also enabled native fetch on SSR using `withFetch()`. Once after deployment of  the upgraded application we encountered permanent memory  increase and finally the application restarting due to OOM. 

After investigating it became obvious that the heap space size only got exceeded when using native node fetch. Removing `withFetch()` fixed the problem. Below find a screeshot from Datadog monitoring, which nicely shows what happened over the past weeks.

![app_heap_space_usage_graph_4_weeks](https://github.com/angular/angular/assets/48031693/7e0713f8-b5d8-4047-ab50-2d24263606ad)

In order to exclude a dependency to the node version , we tried with several versions from v20 up to recent v22. The behaviour when using native fetch was reproducible.

Assuming that native node fetch will very likely become standard in future NG versions and the polyfill will become removed, this makes me a bit nervous when seeing our massive problems while using native fetch!

I won't provide a repo at this point, as it requires time preparing it and I am not sure if it will add value, because
* the issue is so obvious it actually must be known already (even though I'm wondering I didn't find anything related)
* I'm not fully sure if it is even related to Angular but rather a bug in node / undici implementation (found a lot of not cleaned up undici Timeout references between heap size snapshots)
* when providing a repro, the memory footprint for such example app is much smaller than with our enterprise app, so it will only be possible to recognize a memory increase by taking multiple memory snapshots while app is requesting data and comparing new instances created but not cleaned up between 2 snapshots.

That's why I first wanna post this issue in hope someone already knows the issue and might have an idea or direction what's causing it or even how to fix it. If still a repro would be required, let me know and I will try to provide one.

Kind regards,
Tobias

--

comments:
This reminds me of #55396 with a fix that will land in 18.1 (#55530). 
Can you make sure that optimization are enable on your prod build ? (for example you could check if the `ng` global is present on the browser console).

The above fix that was mentioned by @JeanMeche is included in 17.3.7. @vz-tl it unclear from your comments if you are using the application or server Angular CLI builder. Can you please share your `angular.json`?

The configuration appears correct since both settings have `optimization` set to `true`. I trust that `@angular-builders/custom-webpack:server` is applying the appropriate options for the production configuration. Additionally, I recommend updating to the latest version of `@angular`, or at least to the latest patch, to see if the issue persists.

To further investigate this problem, we need a minimal reproduction. Could you please set one up?

You can read [here](https://github.com/angular/angular/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md#-submitting-an-issue) why this is necessary. A good way to create a minimal reproduction is to generate a new app using `ng new repro-app`, add the minimal code required to replicate the issue, then push this repository to GitHub and share the link here.

@alan-agius4 , here we go: https://github.com/vz-tl/ng-fetch-leakage-repro

Please have a look at the README.md I created with instructions how to test. There's a test script which fires 1000 requests against the running app. The app itself will request from a publicly accessible testing API, by using HttpClient.  Usually, I always run the test script 3-5 times in a row, after each time saving a memory snapshot.

Let's get one thing out of the way: I'm definitely not an expert in  debugging memory leaks! :D  Chrome inspector still is somewhat double Dutch to me, but I tried my best to read something out of the memory snapshots.

Obviously, this super-tiny example app likely will never run OOM, compared to our real app, which of course has a much bigger memory footprint. But at least I see a clear tendency:

- using `withFetch()` seems to increase the heap size much more than without.
- there are are much more not removed instances like `Document2`, `R3Injector`, `core_NGZone` (which looks to me they could belong to not garbage collected application instances)
- quite obvious is the amount of `undici` Timeout references, wich is not present at all when not using node fetch. Not sure those leftover could be cause by a  bug with native fetch leading to leakage.

I'd be glad if you could have a look and I hope I'm not totally on the wrong track.

@vz-tl, thanks for the reproduction. The first thing I noticed is that you are generating a development build. I switched to using the production build with `ng run leakage-repro-app:server:production` and ran the tests along with several memory snapshots. After running the tests four times, the memory usage remained around 14.1-14.3 MB. I also switched to using `XHR` instead of `fetch`, and the memory usage stayed within this range as well.
 
It's important to manually force garbage collection (GC) before taking memory snapshots. Can you confirm if you're doing this?

When handling numerous requests, it's normal for memory usage to increase and stay elevated; this doesn't necessarily indicate a memory leak. V8 tends to delay memory cleanup under CPU pressure until it's absolutely necessary, often after transferring memory to the old space.

I noticed in your screenshot that the memory usage reaches 640 MB, leading to an OOM. Assuming your production environment is running in a container, ensure that the `--max-old-space-size` aligns with the container's memory limit. Otherwise, the application might encounter out-of-memory (OOM) errors.

Hi @alan-agius4 ,

Sorry! You're right, I missed adding the prod parameter to the build command! 

However, I fixed it, updated the repo and re-ran the tests as I did before with below results. And of course, I always hit "Collect Garbage" before taking a snapshot!

## with fetch:

![heap_snapshots_withFetch](https://github.com/angular/angular/assets/48031693/960eed11-2ade-43e5-a0cd-51723d58585a)

- Document2: 5 instances
- core_NgZone:  4 instances
- R3Injector: 8 instances
- Timeout:  5990 instances <---- very suspicious! the timeouts are referring to `node:internal/deps/undici/undici` which is related to native node fetch!

## without fetch:
![heap_snapshots_without_fetch](https://github.com/angular/angular/assets/48031693/eff39a28-c937-41b0-bede-b4d681df6762)

- Document2: 2 instances
- core_NgZone:  1 instance
- R3Injector: 2 instances
- Timeout:  1 instance

Based on my tests, there still is a clear difference! Without using fetch I always got and get less memory consumption and less leftover instances compared to when using withFetch.

As I said, my knowledge about debugging memory leaks isn't great, however I'd say I'm meanwhile experienced enough in developing and running an enterprise-grade Angular app with server-side rendering since > 5 years. So I'm quite convinced we're running our prod app appropriately configured. This should also apply for aligning `--max-old-space-size` with container limits, which has been proven to work successfully in the past as we never encountered OOM errors (apart from obviously being caused by regular candidates like unsubscribed subscriptions etc., which always have been identified and fixed accordingly).

But as you can clearly see in my initial screenshot from Datadog, the memory leakage resulting in a OOM started immediately with deploying an application build including `withFetch()`. And the OOM errors and leakage stopped immediately after deploying a version where we only reverted this change! So to me it is absolutely clear that the OOM restarts were cause just by withFetch! Since we reverted the change we had several newer deployments and the app still is running flawlessly without any memory increase! 

I'm really out of ideas meanwhile, how to debug and how to additionally prove that `withFetch()` is the culprit! At least this still remains quite obvious to me.

We also have an Angular (18.0.3) SSR production app which has a memory leak we haven't been able to resolve. We added `withFetch()` in January, but I'm not sure if we had memory issues before that. We'll remove `withFetch()` and see if it makes a difference in our app. We are using the `@angular-devkit/build-angular:browser` and `@angular-devkit/build-angular:server` builders.

@vz-tl, I looked at it again and successfully replicated the issue with your reproduction. I'm not sure why I couldn't see it before. Unfortunately, I didn't have time to investigate further today, but I'll continue looking into it in the coming days.
Please note that zone 0.14.8 has been released and should land a fix for the memory leak.
Thx for the work, @alan-agius4 ! Will report back ASAP!

Tests on staging system went successfully. However, due to not being able to simulate same load as on prod, a final verification will only be possible once we deployed to production. Still I'm confident the issue is fixed now. Thx again to all involved!
